uncited: This family provides methods to map scalar volume data to opacity and integrate these values along viewing rays using piecewise linear approximations.
It solves the problem of efficiently computing the volume rendering integral while allowing for flexible, user-defined opacity mappings that can be linearly interpolated between control points.

It differs from its siblings by focusing on the structural linearity of the transfer function or the density field to enable analytical integration or simple interpolation, whereas [Alpha-to-Weight Computation (Forward)](2373-alpha-to-weight-computation-forward.md) focuses on weight computation and [SDF-based Opacity Derivation via Logistic CDF](3233-sdf-based-opacity-derivation-via-logistic-cdf.md) uses probabilistic models.
The family operates on the scalar field $V(\mathbf{p})$ sampled at positions $\mathbf{p}$ along the ray.
These values are subsequently used in the front-to-back compositing equation defined in [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md).
The concept of piecewise linear transfer functions has been widely adopted in volume rendering to provide intuitive control over visualization parameters.
